senses.gloss: m. pl. (pl. of κομμενταρήσιος, S. = commentariensis) those having charge of public records, esp. registrars of prisoners, jailers (v. Sm. Ant. s. v. Commentarius).
units: <cite ref="Gittin 28b:12">Gitt. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>מק׳ של נכרים וכ׳</he> if one heard from gentile jailers, ‘such and such a man is dead’, ‘such and such a man has been put to death’, you cannot allow his wife to marry again; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 16:5:2">Y. Yeb. XVI, 15ᵈ</cite> <he>מקֹמַנְטְרִיסֵי המלך</he> from the (Roman) king’s jailers.
